claim: Let \(Y_1,Y_2,Y_3\) be iid, non-atomic, nondegenerate and symmetric real random variables, \(T_j=\sum_{i=1}^jY_i\), and \(A_i=|Y_i|\). Put \(t=\mathbb P(A_1>A_2+A_3)\). Then \(0\le t<1/3\), and the exact joint law of \((\operatorname{sgn}T_1,\operatorname{sgn}T_2,\operatorname{sgn}T_3)\) has word probabilities \(P(+++) = P(---)=5/16\), \(P(++-)=P(--+)=1/16\), \(P(+-+)=P(-+-)=1/16-t/8\), and \(P(+--)=P(-++)=1/16+t/8\). Every \(t\in[0,1/3)\) is attained by an absolutely continuous symmetric increment law; this is the complete sharp feasible family. As a concrete application, the three odd-time signs of the ascent-descent walk of a uniform permutation on seven symbols correspond to triangular increments, for which \(t=19/90\), and their joint law differs from the corresponding five-step fair simple-random-walk sign law by total variation distance exactly \(7/720\), although their three-step occupation-count laws agree.

correctness.rationale: Each symmetric atomless increment factors into independent fair sign and positive magnitude. Exhaustive analytic conditioning on three signs gives the eight probabilities with sole parameter t=P(A1>A2+A3). Dominance events are disjoint, with strict upper bound since iid draws can fall in a short multiplicative interval; bounded ratio gives t=0, while a continuous log-uniform magnitude family gives every t<1/3 by continuity and a largest-gap limit. Tang's torus transform reduces the three permutation odd-time signs to iid triangular increments. Exact polynomial integration yields t=19/90 and an exhaustive 6! versus 2^5 rational calculation confirms total variation 7/720. Independently replayed script verifies the displayed finite arithmetic; universal assertions are analytical, not inferred from enumeration.
